coverageNotes:
Methodology note: this session's WebSearch tool hit an apparent session cap after only ~24 queries (far short of the usual 200), so after the initial country-by-country sweep (which covered the Gulf states, Egypt, South Africa, Nigeria, Kenya, and the core Australia/NZ brands) I switched to WebFetch against Wikipedia's convention lists and candidate official domains for the rest, plus an unsuccessful attempt to use search-engine result pages via WebFetch as a substitute (Bing/Google returned irrelevant/cached content). That shaped the remaining gaps:

- Jordan, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Morocco: no convention could be confirmed against the attendee/guest-lineup bar with a working official site. Leads exist but weren't verifiable: a "Muscat Nights" Comic Con announced by Muscat Municipality in Oman, social-media-only "Comic Con Lebanon" mentions, and a defunct IGN Convention that ran in both Dubai and Manama 2013-2016. Excluded rather than guessed.
- Sub-Saharan Africa beyond Nigeria (Lagos), Kenya (Nairobi/Mombasa), South Africa and Egypt is thin. Algeria's long-running Algiers comics festival (FIBDA/Algiers International Comics Festival) could not be confirmed as still active - Wikipedia's own infobox links to bdalger.net, which now resolves to an unrelated product-management login page, and no 2024-2026 edition news turned up - so it was dropped rather than published on stale/unverifiable data. Ghana, Tanzania, Uganda, Zimbabwe (a Harare "OtakuKon" anime festival surfaced in one secondary snippet but could not be verified), Ethiopia, DRC, Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire and Tunisia were not confirmed either way. An "Ibadan Fan Expo" (Nigeria) surfaced on an African-conventions directory but its page 404'd; a "Rendacon" (Lagos) and "Comic Panel Awards" turned out to be an animation-industry summit and an awards show respectively, not fan conventions, so both were left out.
- Pacific Island nations (Fiji, Papua New Guinea, etc.): nothing found.
- Australia/NZ is the best-covered part of the region (19 AU + 4 NZ entries) but is still missing some likely-real niche events whose official domains I couldn't pin down with confidence, so they were excluded rather than guessed: NZ's "Overload" (Auckland anime con) and "Wellycon"; Australian tabletop-specific cons such as Cancon; a Melbourne SF con ("Continuum"); and horror-specific cons (a "Monster Fest" domain is now parked/for sale). Saudi Arabia's Trofee-sponsored "TCG Con Arabia" (Riyadh, trading cards/collectibles, Feb 2026) and a biennial Bahrain gaming con called "AFK" were both found but dropped for lack of a confirmed official URL - worth a follow-up pass.
- Judgment call: Riyadh's giant esports festival (formerly "Gamers8", now folded into the global "Esports World Cup") was excluded as a professional esports tournament rather than a fan convention with a comics/creator/cosplay guest lineup - worth reconsidering if the project wants esports festivals in scope.
- A handful of included entries carry date/URL uncertainty flagged in their own notes (Comic Con Arabia, QuantumCon Kuwait, Olamot Convention, SwanCon, Bahrain Comic Con, CairoComix, Nairobi/Mombasa Comic Con, and the Perth/Adelaide Oz Comic-Con and Tauranga Armageddon stops) and deserve a confirmation pass before publishing live.

coverageNotes: Strong coverage of Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Benelux, the Nordics, Poland, Czechia, Hungary, the Balkans, Greece, Cyprus, the Baltics and Malta via Wikipedia convention lists plus the RosterCon aggregator (which conveniently exposes each event's own official-site link, letting me verify ~90 URLs directly). Weak spots: (1) Estonia — no qualifying convention found at all; (2) Ukraine — Comic Con Ukraine/Kyiv Comic Con has no confirmed edition since 2021 (2022 explicitly cancelled for the war, 2023+ unclear) and the "FANCON" successor's most recent confirmed date was 2024, so both were left out as likely-defunct rather than guessed at; (3) Belarus, Moldova, North Macedonia, Bosnia, Montenegro, Albania, Kosovo, Luxembourg — no qualifying public fan event surfaced; these may simply have none, or may have small/undocumented ones I couldn't find. (4) Germany has a very long tail (a 30-page aggregator listing) of small single-franchise celebrity-signing weekends (Harry Potter-, Stranger Things-, Star Wars-themed, etc., mostly from a handful of touring organizers) beyond the ~16 I included — real conventions with real guest lineups, but I sampled the larger/more distinctive ones rather than cataloguing all of them. (5) Furry conventions are thin outside Germany/Sweden/Poland — I could not verify any dedicated Russian, Turkish, or Balkan furry con. (6) Horror and toy/collectible-only conventions are generally thin region-wide; most horror and toy content in this region shows up folded into multigenre comic-cons rather than as standalone events. (7) WebSearch ran out of budget partway through the task (200/200 used), so the back half of the research relied on WebFetch against Wikipedia, RosterCon, FurryCons/FurryGuides, and official sites directly — thorough, but it means a few entries (Liburnicon's current activity, Desucon's exact month, IgroMir's and Istanbul Comic Con's official domains, which returned bot-blocked 403s rather than confirmable content) carry more uncertainty than the rest and are flagged in their notes. No Western/Southern European countries (UK, France, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Ireland) were researched, as they fall outside this assignment's region.

coverageNotes:
Region = Canada, Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean, and South America. This session's WebSearch tool was exhausted after roughly 23 queries (hit a hard 200/200-call session cap almost immediately — it appears the cap is shared across the parallel region-agents in this workflow run), so nearly all research had to proceed via WebFetch only: fetching Wikipedia pages/Wikipedia-internal-search, and testing guessed organizer domains directly. Most third-party search/aggregator routes I tried to substitute (DuckDuckGo, Bing, Startpage, Mojeek, Ecosia, 10times.com) came back as CAPTCHAs, 403s, or useless geo-mismatched results, and many plausible LatAm domains failed outright (DNS/cert errors) even when the convention itself is real, per Wikipedia. I did not invent a URL for anything I couldn't get a tool to actually load.

Strong coverage: Canada (all major Fan Expo HQ shows, anime cons, SF cons, furry cons, horror con, and tabletop cons I could find, spanning ON/QC/BC/AB/MB/NS/SK) and Brazil (São Paulo/Belo Horizonte/Rio majors). Moderate coverage: Mexico (Mexico City only — La Mole, CCXP MX, Electronic Game Show; could not confirm a working official URL for Guadalajara, Monterrey, or Tijuana shows, or for any Mexican toy/anime-specific/furry con, despite several attempts and evidence some exist, e.g. FESTO Cómic), Argentina (Rosario + Buenos Aires only; Buenos Aires's well-known "Comicópolis" convention could not be matched to a working domain and was dropped), Colombia (Bogotá + Medellín editions of one brand; no other cities confirmed).

Essentially uncovered, despite real attempts: Chile (Wikipedia confirms a recurring "Comic Con Chile" at Espacio Riesco, Santiago, but no official URL could be found), Peru, Ecuador, Venezuela, Bolivia, Paraguay, and Uruguay (its one documented convention, "Continuará...", has been defunct since 2011 — no live replacement found). All of Central America except Costa Rica and Panama (Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Belize — no confirmed events). All Caribbean nations except Puerto Rico: the Dominican Republic's "Dominicana Comic-Con" site exists but shows no sign of a 2025/2026 edition (still branded "DCC2019") so it was excluded as likely inactive; Jamaica, Trinidad & Tobago, Cuba, and the Bahamas were not confirmed at all. No furry, tabletop-gaming, or horror convention could be confirmed anywhere in Latin America/Caribbean outside Canada — these genres may exist regionally but I found no verifiable official sites. A few Canadian shows I have reasonable evidence are real but dropped for lack of a working official URL: CAN-CON (Ottawa, literary SF) and Animaritime (Fredericton, NB, anime). Three URLs (Winnipeg Comiccon, Ottawa Comiccon, Toronto Comicon) are the organizer's standard domain pattern but could not be re-confirmed live due to a repeated tool error on the final check — everything else listed was directly loaded and read this session.

coverageNotes:
Region covered: TX, OK, NM, AZ, CO, UT, NV, ID, MT, WY. Delivered 73 entries, short of the "well over a hundred" target for a region this size — mainly because this session's WebSearch quota (shared across what appears to be a larger multi-region workflow run) was exhausted after about 18 queries, early in the research. From that point on I relied on WebFetch against Wikipedia, official convention sites, and the RosterCon.com per-state listings — fancons.com/furrycons.com returned 403 on every query (bot-blocked), WikiFur.com was unreachable (connection resets), and DuckDuckGo required a CAPTCHA, so several discovery avenues the task suggested were closed off.

Weakest coverage: WYOMING has zero entries — the only two leads found (Wyoming Pop Culture Con in Casper, last confirmed April 2024; Anime 307 in Cheyenne, last confirmed September 2025) have no locatable official website and no confirmed 2026/2027 date, so neither clears the "never invent a URL" bar. IDAHO (3) and MONTANA (3) are almost certainly under-covered rather than genuinely sparse. Toy/collectible shows and pure tabletop-gaming meetups are under-covered everywhere, since small one-day shows rarely surface outside hyper-local calendars that search would normally find.

Named events found but excluded for lack of a verifiable official URL (worth a manual follow-up pass): Big Texas Comicon (San Antonio), Beaumont Comic Con, Tip O' Texas Comic Con (South Padre Island), TerrorFest (Conroe TX), Pony Friends Forever (San Antonio, brony), KimoKawaii (Conroe anime), Alamo City Furry Invasion (San Marcos), Texas Furry Siesta (Dallas), Wild Furloween West (Fort Worth), Anthro Weekend Utah (Layton), OneAnime Con (Salt Lake City), Anime Island (Norman OK), Enid Comic Con (OK), Toon Fusion (OK/NM touring brand), Tulsa Comic Con Halloween, Anime Arizona (Mesa), Tucson Comic-Con (domain parked/under construction), Furry Legends of Paradise (Mt. Charleston NV), Elko Cosmic Con (NV), Idaho Falls Retro X4, Anime ID (Caldwell ID), and All C's Collector's Showcase (Aurora CO).

Confirmed defunct / excluded for that reason: Space City Con (Houston — official site now entirely past-tense/archived), ApolloCon (Houston — domain unreachable, no event since ~2015), ConDFW (its old domain is now squatted by an unrelated travel site; no event since 2019), LepreCon (Phoenix — no confirmed edition since 2017-2021), Starfest (Denver — domain not found, believed defunct), Anime Banzai (Layton UT — confirmed ended 2024), RTX Austin itself (ended 2023 when Rooster Teeth shut down; its community successor Homebrew Austin is included instead), and Wizard World (sold its remaining shows to FAN EXPO HQ in 2021; no current stop in this region). AggieCon (Texas A&M, College Station) was also left out despite a long history — I could not confirm current activity or find an official site this session.

A handful of included entries carry residual uncertainty, flagged in their own "note" field, where a plausible official domain returned an HTTP 403/expired-certificate (suggesting a real but bot-blocked site) rather than a page I could actually read: GenghisCon, TactiCon, DenFur, Oni-Con, PokeKon, and OAFCon. Multi-city brands (DarknessCon, Creation Entertainment, GalaxyCon, FAN EXPO, Mad Monster) were each split into one entry per city per the task's instruction. Deliberately excluded as non-matching: single-guest retail signing events (e.g. "The Hive HQ" appearances in North Richland Hills, TX), DEF CON Las Vegas (hacker/security con, no fit among the ten listed genres), and Renaissance-faire-type events (different genre, not one of the ten types).

That likely under-represents small, local, or Wikipedia-invisible shows - especially one-off hotel-ballroom comic/toy/collectible shows with no Wikipedia page and no easily-guessable domain. Delaware: despite extensive targeted searching, no currently-active qualifying convention could be found actually based in Delaware (Thy Geekdom Con was Wilmington-based 2015-2017 but relocated to Oaks, PA in 2018, where it remains) - this looks like a genuine gap rather than only a search artifact. Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont, and West Virginia each yielded only 1 confirmed entry; these are small/low-population states so this may partly reflect real scarcity. Left out as defunct, on hiatus, or unverifiable despite some evidence of past existence: AnimeNEXT (Edison NJ, indefinite hiatus since 2023), Vericon (Cambridge MA, defunct since 2016), the original DexCon (Morristown NJ, superseded by DexLite), Genericon (Troy NY, defunct), Anime Mid-Atlantic (Norfolk VA, hiatus since 2019), Universal Fan Con (Baltimore MD, failed 2018 one-off), Chessiecon (MD, official domain now redirects to an unrelated site), HELIOsphere (NY/NJ, 2025 cancelled, no 2026 announcement), Albany Comic Con (NY, no evidence found past the 1970s-80s), Vermont Fan Fest (Burlington VT, official domain is dead), Chiller Theatre Expo (Secaucus NJ, could not confirm continued operation post-2019/20), Eerie Con (location/status unverifiable; site had an expired certificate), ColossalCon East (PA, cancelled 2020, no confirmed return), Supermegafest (MA, site unreachable), FlightSimCon (Windsor Locks CT, confirmed defunct), Long Island Comic Con/LICF (unverifiable), and notably Tekko (Pittsburgh PA's well-known anime convention) - its tekko.org domain is now a parked/for-sale page and no 2023+ activity could be confirmed, so it was left out despite being a significant regional con; it may still be running under a URL this session could not locate. Region = US Southeast: NC, SC, GA, FL, AL, MS, TN, KY, AR, LA. 89 entries. Important process note: the WebSearch tool's 200-call session budget was exhausted partway through Georgia research, before Florida, Alabama, Mississippi, Tennessee, Kentucky, Arkansas, and Louisiana could get the same live-search treatment as NC/SC/GA. From that point on, research relied on Wikipedia (list pages, "Category:Conventions in [state]" pages, and individual convention articles, all freely fetchable) plus direct WebFetch verification of official-site URLs; fancons.com/animecons.com/furrycons.com/horrorcons.com and several search engines (DuckDuckGo, Bing) actively block automated fetches (403/CAPTCHA), so their aggregator listings could only be used via the WebSearch summaries gathered before the cap hit. A lucky break - finding that regional promoter VXV Events (vxvevents.com/events) runs ~10 small comic-con/anime-fest/card-show brands across AR/MS/AL/TN, and that "Anime Town Cons" runs shows in AL/SC/FL/LA/MS - meaningfully filled in Alabama, Mississippi, Arkansas, and the Memphis, TN gap that remained after the search budget ran out.

Per instructions, no URL was ever invented: every entry's url was actually fetched and confirmed (or, for ~8 small shows with no independent domain, the url points to the verified organizer homepage - e.g. VXV Events, SCARAB's tabletop.events listing, Tampa Toy Con's Eventeny page - noted in each entry's "note"). Many conventions' own sites had already rolled over to a confirmed 2027 date by this Oct 2026 research date; these still clear the "ran 2025/2026 or announced 2026/2027" bar and are flagged in their notes.

Known gaps / things I could not verify and so left out, rather than guess a URL: NC's Oak City Mini Con, Wake Forest Comic-Con, Amazing Art Expo Charlotte, ReCon (Kernersville tabletop), Quest Con (Garner tabletop), Mythic Con (Charlotte tabletop), Charlotte Anime-Fest, Asheville Anime-Fest; SC's Charleston Anime-Fest, Charleston Horror-Fest, CharlestonCon (North Charleston), Columbia Anime-Fest, VillainSCon, ShushCon; GA's DaggerCon, Rangerstop & Pop Con, Valdosta Comic Con, Atlanta Comic Convention (the small recurring one, distinct from Collect-A-Con), Decepta Con; FL's Tropicon and OASIS (Orlando-area literary SF cons run by local clubs) and a Tampa-area "Necronomicon"; and SC's Banzaicon, which I confirmed is now explicitly paused. Alabama and Mississippi remain the thinnest-covered states - Montgomery, Auburn, and the Gulf Coast of MS beyond Biloxi/Jackson turned up nothing verifiable, and Huntsville AL's Con†Stellation is confirmed defunct (no events since 2015) so was excluded despite a stray travel-guide mention suggesting otherwise. Louisiana outside New Orleans (Baton Rouge, Shreveport, Lafayette) and a general-audience Louisville, KY comic con (ConGlomeration/Derby City Comic Con/Louisville Supercon/GalaxyCon Louisville all confirmed ended by 2019-2020) turned up nothing currently active. Chattanooga, TN lost Chattacon (organizers announced no further editions in Aug 2025) with no confirmed replacement. DeepSouthCon (a rotating regional SF con) is active but its 2026 host is Dallas, TX (outside this region) with no 2027 host confirmed yet, so it was excluded this cycle. Given the search-budget constraint, there are very likely additional small one-day/library-run shows in this region, especially in AL, MS, and rural LA/AR, that never surfaced in Wikipedia or the organizer sites I found.

coverageNotes:
Methodology note: this session's shared WebSearch budget (pooled across concurrent region agents in this workflow) was exhausted after ~30 queries, early in the Japan/Korea/China phase. The remainder of the research was done via WebFetch against Wikipedia (List of anime/comic/multigenre/gaming/furry/sci-fi/horror/toy conventions, plus country and topic categories), RosterCon.com, and organizers' own sites, with Bing/DuckDuckGo search fetches largely blocked by CAPTCHA/geo-redirect. This is slower and less complete than live web search, especially for sources not well indexed in English.

Well covered: Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia, Philippines, and India (Comic Con India's city-by-city 2026 schedule was confirmed directly from its own site plus RosterCon's per-city pages).

Gaps/weak spots by country:
- Macau: no public fan convention of any kind could be found; likely genuinely has none of scale.
- Pakistan: Wikipedia's "Pakistani comics" article names Karachi Comic Con, "Comic Con PK," ComicCon Lahore, and TwinCon, but all citations date to 2016-2018 and no 2025/2026 activity or official website could be confirmed with available tools, so none are included despite likely still existing in some form.
- Bangladesh: Dhaka Pop Culture Expo (2013-2017) is explicitly tagged defunct on Wikipedia. The Bangladesh Association of Cosplayers sends representatives to the World Cosplay Summit, showing an active cosplay community, but no public flagship convention was found.
- Nepal and Sri Lanka: no conventions turned up in Wikipedia or any aggregator checked; this reads as a genuine absence of large-scale organized fandom events rather than a search failure.
- China: likely undercounted outside Shanghai/Guangzhou/Hangzhou. Beijing, Shenzhen, and Chengdu almost certainly have ACG events but none could be confirmed; China's tabletop-gaming and furry convention scenes (Wikipedia names only one furry con region-wide, Shanghai's "Super Furry Fusion," semiannual since 2018) could not be given a verified official URL and were excluded on that basis.
- South Korea: SICAF (Seoul International Cartoon & Animation Festival) and PlayX4 (Gyeonggi-do's game show, 130,000+ attendees) are real, large, active events, but no official website could be confirmed through available tools (domain guesses failed or were inconclusive), so both are excluded.
- Vietnam/Indonesia: several additional small doujin markets and the Vietnam-Japan Comic Fes (VJCF) are documented but lack a confirmed stable homepage.
- Excluded as confirmed inactive/defunct (not just unverified): Asia Pop Comic Convention Manila (inactive since 2018-19), Comics Fest India (defunct), Dhaka Pop Culture Expo (defunct), Hellofest Indonesia (site unreachable, status unclear), Asia Game Show Hong Kong (defunct).
- Excluded for lack of a stable official homepage despite apparently being real/recurring: Singapore's Doujin Market, Doki Doki Anime Market, Cos Haven, and Randamu World (Eventbrite/Instagram-only); Thailand's BKK Comics Art Festival; Shanghai's Super Furry Fusion.
- No scifi- or horror-specific convention with a fixed yearly homepage was found anywhere in the region (Japan's Nihon SF Taikai rotates host committee/city annually with no permanent site; Chengdu's 2023 Worldcon was a one-off, not recurring).

coverageNotes:
Methodology: discovery via Wikipedia convention lists, FanCons/AnimeCons aggregator search snippets, and organizer sites (FAN EXPO HQ, ReedPop, Strategicon, GalaxyCon, Comic-Con International, etc.), then every entry's official URL, dates and status were verified directly (WebFetch of the convention's own site, or a live Google search read through a real browser) before inclusion. This session's WebSearch tool quota was exhausted after only ~6 queries (apparently a shared/session-wide budget), so almost all verification after that point was done via direct site fetches and a Chrome-browser Google-search workaround rather than the WebSearch tool itself - this made the process slower and means some very small/obscure events were likely missed.

Result: 78 active conventions across CA (49), OR (6... actually 8), WA (15), AK (2), HI (4). California in particular has such a dense convention calendar (many one-day city-specific comic/anime/horror/gaming shows) that this list, while large, is very unlikely to be complete - especially for small Central Valley, Inland Empire, and smaller Bay Area towns.

Confirmed EXCLUDED as defunct/dormant/out-of-bar (not invented, actively checked): Califur and ConFurence (furry, defunct since ~2017-18), SiliCon/Silicon Valley Comic Con (defunct 2023, succeeded by GalaxyCon San Jose, which IS included), Pacific Media Expo (no event found since 2022), Alternative Press Expo (ended 2017), Crunchyroll Expo (on hiatus since 2023, no announced return), GaymerX (defunct since 2019), SpoCon (discontinued 2022), Gaylaxicon (hasn't been held on the West Coast since 2004), IndieCade (no confirmed in-person event since ~2022), Astronomicon (turns out to be in Ypsilanti, Michigan, not Sacramento - a self-correction), Northwest Pinball and Arcade Show (its old domain now redirects to an unrelated business).

Could NOT verify well enough to include (real events that may still be active, but no confirmed official URL/current date was found - worth re-checking with a full web-search budget): Santa Rosa Comic Con, San Jose Con, Super-Con, Mouse-Con (a small family of one-day NorCal comic shows sharing a promoter/phone number; last confirmed dates were 2019-2023), Monterey Bay Comic Con, Fresno Comic Con (separate from Hauntmare Expo, which IS included), MikomiCon (Northridge, CA anime con - site unreachable), Faerieworlds (Eugene, OR fantasy/arts festival - unclear whether it still clears the fan-con guest-lineup bar), Gaslight Gathering (San Diego steampunk - site had a certificate error), East Bay Board Game Convention (appears to exist only on the shared tabletop.events ticketing platform, no independent official site found), Days of the Dead LA, Nerdbot Con.

Weak spots by design/population, not by omission: furry and tabletop conventions are genuinely thin outside the SF Bay Area, LA and Seattle metro areas - no furry con was found in Oregon, Alaska or Hawaii, and dedicated toy/collectible-only shows are rare (only the Collect-A-Con tour stops qualified). Alaska and Hawaii coverage (2 and 4 entries respectively) is believed to be close to complete given those states' small populations, but was checked with fewer search angles than California. Sizes/attendance figures for most mid-size and smaller entries are estimates from general knowledge, not confirmed attendance reports.

coverageNotes:
Methodology and major constraint: this session's WebSearch tool was capped at 200 calls total and was already exhausted (200/200) after only ~18 searches on my side — the cap is evidently shared across all the parallel per-region subagents in this workflow run, not per-session. I pivoted almost entirely to WebFetch: Wikipedia list/category pages and individual convention infoboxes (which often include an explicit "Website" field I queried directly), plus direct fetches of official convention sites. I also smoke-tested generic web search via curl (DuckDuckGo showed a bot CAPTCHA; Bing returned unrelated localized results) and found those unusable, and found several ordinary aggregator sites (fancons.com, wikifur.com, fancyclopedia.org, animecons.com) actively blocked (403/connection-reset) from this sandbox. Every entry's URL above was either successfully fetched this session or cross-confirmed via a Wikipedia infobox/table; a handful (flagged in their own "note") rely on strong prior knowledge because the live fetch was blocked by DNS/TLS errors that also affected domains independently confirmed correct by Wikipedia (e.g. bdangouleme.com) — i.e. sandbox network flakiness, not evidence the URL is wrong — so treat those specific few as medium- rather than high-confidence and worth a quick spot check before publishing.

Confirmed defunct/discontinued and deliberately excluded: EGX as a standalone show (its own site now folds it into MCM Comic Con for 2026), Nine Worlds Geekfest (ended 2018, no revival found), GameForce (gameforce.nl now resolves to an unrelated Eindhoven game shop), Expomanga Madrid (Wikipedia confirms it was cancelled starting 2019), ScareCON (explicitly a trade-only scare-attraction show), Dimension Jump (its listed .info domain is now squatted by an unrelated gambling site).

Dropped rather than guessed a URL: Dublin Comic Con (could not confirm current status either way), Stunfest/Rennes, CAPTION/Oxford, Strip Turnhout/Belgium, the regional Spanish "Heroes Comic Con" chain (A Coruña/Vigo/Málaga/Marbella), and the UK Showmasters-family celebrity-guest shows Destination Star Trek, Sci-Fi Scarborough, For the Love of Horror and Memorabilia (NEC) — only their sibling "For The Love Of Sci-Fi" had a confirmable official URL (via a Wikipedia infobox). Japan Expo Sud (Marseille) and Japan Expo Belgium (Brussels) are real sister events per Wikipedia but their likely subdomain URLs actively failed DNS (unlike the sibling "paris." subdomain, which resolved fine), so I left them out rather than publish a probably-wrong link. AmeCon, Minamicon, EM-Con, Hispacon (no single stable host — a different club runs it each year) and several small Belgian/French/Dutch/Swiss/Irish furry meetups named only in passing by a search snippet (AnthroTales, Flüüfff, CanthroFur, Ainmhícon, Dutch FurCon, Furry Weekend Holland, Golden Leaves Con, etc.) were dropped for the same reason.

Weak spots to flag for whoever merges regions: Luxembourg yielded zero qualifying events despite effort (it may genuinely have none at this scale). Belgium (3) and the Netherlands (5) are likely under-covered. Furry is represented only by ConFuzzled (UK) and toys only by ToyCon UK (UK) — both genres are almost certainly under-covered across France/Italy/Spain/Netherlands/Switzerland. Tabletop gaming outside the UK/Ireland is thin. Spain and Italy almost certainly have more second-tier regional manga/comic salons (e.g. more Japan Weekend cities, more Italian city comic fairs) than I could individually verify. All "size" tiers are best-effort from whatever attendance figure I could find and may mix different source years.
